Unblinding review: specimen was bryostatin (PubChem CID 6435419) annotated in BBBC021 as Kinase inhibitors; ChEMBL has no curated mechanism. Conclusion Kinase inhibitors was correct by code.

Reflection: Profile showed early low-dose isolated chromatin decondensation (nuc_dna_mean z -5.2 at 0.1 µM, -8.2 at 10 µM, rho -0.80) without mitotic arrest (frac_mitotic_like rho -0.11) or tubulin/actin bundling, which argued against Aurora / microtubule stabilizer primary MoA despite late high-dose actin/tubulin texture increase (act_glcm_contrast z 29.0, tub_glcm_contrast 10.6 at 10 µM - secondary toxicity). reflection.text:
Unblinded compound bryostatin, PubChem CID 6435419, ChEMBL no curated MoA, name/structure agree per e16-e17. Verdict correct but low-confidence: truth Kinase inhibitors, agent Kinase inhibitors p=0.52, approved on review. 

What got right: The dose-stratified acquisition was discriminative. Listing showed 8 doses 0.003-10 uM, 4 wells budget (e1). Sampling 1 uM (e2: nuc_dna_mean z=-7.8, nuc_eccentricity z=-7.6, cell_solidity z=-5.2, 420 cells) and 10 uM (e3: act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0, act_std z=+16.3, tub_glcm_contrast z=+10.6, 249 cells) first captured onset vs maximal effect, then adding 0.1 uM (e7: nuc_dna_mean z=-5.2, 715 cells) and 0.3 uM (e8: nuc_dna_mean z=-5.0, act_glcm_contrast z=-3.0, 1643 cells) revealed the transition. Key was isolated DNA decondensation at low dose without cytoskeletal changes (e7/e8 vs e3), plus flat mitotic signal (e10: frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.11 p=0.89 over 4 wells). This argued against Aurora kinase inhibitors despite microscopist candidates at both high dose (e4: density lower, Aurora/Actin disruptors/Microtubule destabilizers, 9 observations) and intermediate dose (e5: Aurora, 6 observations) and allowed correct weighting of the 4-well NSC vote 3/4 Kinase inhibitors (e9) over the initial 2-well vote 1/2 Microtubule stabilizers (e6). Dose trends rho=+0.80 for tub_glcm_contrast (e11) and frac_large_nucleus (e12) both p=0.20 and rho=-0.80 for nuc_dna_mean (e13) p=0.20 , although underpowered with n=4, supported late bundling/polyploidy only at 1-10 uM and early DNA change - consistent with the rationale that early phenotype is not mitotic arrest and late bundling is secondary toxicity. 

What misled/missed: High-dose actin/tubulin extreme contrasts at 10 uM (e3) and the initial NSC k-neighbours Microtubule stabilizers 4/10 (e6) strongly tempted Microtubule stabilizer/Actin disruptor. Aurora also remained at 0.25 in hypothesis update (e14) because of large nuclei trend (e12) and low cell counts/density loss at high dose (e2, e4). No literature was used pre-unblinding to resolve this; post-unblinding searches (e18-e19) returned PKC-related hits but were not integrated into the conclusion. Literature found now supports the kinase assignment: bryostatin binding to protein kinase C PMID 2001329 and modulation via protein kinase D1 activation PMID 18765827, with broader PKC context PMID 9147607, rather than a direct tubulin/actin mechanism. 

Why the decision held: I discounted the high-dose cytoskeletal phenotype because it was absent at 0.1-0.3 uM where nuc_dna_mean already -5, and because frac_mitotic_like showed no dose dependence, which is inconsistent with primary Aurora inhibition that expects mitotic enrichment and increased ploidy/DNA content early, not decreased DNA intensity. The shift from e6 to e9 after adding low-dose wells was the decisive comparison. Probability 0.52 appropriately reflected remaining conflict from late toxicity with only 4 single-replicate wells acquired.
